details: Russian President Vladimir Putin has signed a comprehensive cryptocurrency regulation law, effective September 1, 2026. This legislation permits the use of Bitcoin and other digital assets for cross-border trade, enabling Russian businesses to conduct international settlements and potentially circumvent Western sanctions. While domestic crypto payments remain prohibited, the law establishes a licensed framework for trading through approved intermediaries, with retail investors facing annual purchase limits and mandatory knowledge tests.
title: Russia Outpaces US in Crypto Regulation: What the New Law Mandates

details: A "crypto Cold War" is unfolding as major global powers like the US, China, and Russia pursue competing strategies regarding digital assets and financial infrastructure. Russia is expanding its digital ruble and experimenting with crypto for foreign trade, while Iran utilizes exchanges and stablecoins to navigate sanctions. China is developing yuan-based payment infrastructure, maintaining a ban on private crypto but fostering a controlled crypto gateway in Hong Kong. These initiatives accelerate the fragmentation of the global payments system, with stablecoins increasingly becoming geopolitical infrastructure, leading to more politicized payments and greater geopolitical risk in the digital currency landscape.
title: Crypto After Sanctions: How Countries Are Building Alternative Financial Networks

details: Bitcoin extended its gains, climbing above the $64,800 level, partly due to easing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Optimism surrounding a potential agreement between Iran and Oman to regulate shipping through the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz has fueled improved appetite for risk assets, including Bitcoin. A diplomatic breakthrough is anticipated to lower crude oil prices, reduce inflation risks, and lessen the need for further Federal Reserve policy tightening, thereby supporting demand for higher-risk assets.
title: Bitcoin extends gains as ETF inflows and Middle East stability boost sentiment

details: A recent Reuters investigation has revealed a sprawling sanctions-evasion network through which an unlicensed Dubai-based crypto exchange, Shelbit, processed billions of dollars. This network is allegedly linked to Iran's central bank, entities tied to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), and illegal gambling operations. At least $676 million from this network reportedly flowed into Binance wallets. Dubai regulators have ordered Shelbit to cease its activities, and US Treasury officials are reviewing the allegations, especially given previous sanctions against Iranian exchanges for facilitating IRGC-linked transactions.
title: Iran-linked exchange sent $676 million to Binance wallets in alleged sanctions-evasion operation: Reuters
